claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Controlled introduction of porosity can reduce the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr without sacrificing its room- or high-temperature mechanical performance.
The proposed intervention is the introduction of controlled porosity.
Introducing controlled porosity will produce a porous microstructure.
Porosity will reduce the overall density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The porous material will retain a coherent high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Retention of a coherent high-entropy-alloy matrix will preserve the alloy's strong mechanical properties despite the introduced porosity.
The porous alloy will have reduced density without a significant loss of yield strength at room temperature.
The porous alloy will have reduced density without a significant loss of yield strength at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of about 855 MPa.
Testing will cover room temperature through 1000 °C under uniaxial compression.
Powder metallurgy or additive manufacturing can be used to introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
A yield-strength decrease greater than 10% is the stipulated threshold for significant degradation.
The optimal porosity level and processing technique are unknown.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires avoiding significant strength loss, but the stated falsification rule rejects a >10% strength loss only when it occurs without a density decrease. Thus, a specimen that loses more than 10% strength while also decreasing in density would violate the predicted outcome but would not falsify the hypothesis under the stated rule.
